moved_judge.question: Why is caching necessary at all? Why not just make the database faster?
Why not let the application query the database directly and keep the architecture simple?
What does caching introduce that you did not have before? What are the costs?
What is the actual intelligence in PhantomCache? Is it AI?
Your tests pass. Does that mean the system is correct and ready?
Walk me through what happens to one request, from the network to the response.
What happens on a cache miss? And what if a thousand clients ask for the same missing key?
What happens when the origin is unavailable?
How do the nodes communicate?
Which node serves a read for a key, and does rendezvous hashing decide that?
Is the dashboard showing real data? And how does the Lab relate to the real system?
Is this deployable in production today? What exists for deployment?
Why not Go or C#? Go has goroutines, a good HTTP server, and is the language of many caches.
Why Tokio, and what does it give you that threads would not?
Why Axum rather than another framework, and why did you write your own HTTP client for the origin?
What are the concurrency implications of your design? Where could it deadlock or stall?
Why rustls and not OpenSSL for the mTLS between nodes? And why do you have both `ring` and `aws-lc-rs`?
Why React with plain CSS and no UI or chart libraries? Isn't that reinventing the wheel?
You have hundreds of tests. Do they prove your concurrent cache is correct?
Why partitioned mutexes? Why not one lock, a lock-free map, or a concurrent hash map crate?
What about lock contention? How do you know it is not a bottleneck?
What stops a cache stampede? What happens to the origin when a hot key expires?
What happens with a hot-key overload? Say one key gets most of the traffic.
How do you know the cache does not leak memory? Is the byte count the real memory use?
Explain epochs. Why not just delete the keys? What does invalidation guarantee?
How does expiry work? What stops the cache from serving very old data? Is the default TTL configurable?
State the time and space complexity of the cache operations.
The origin goes down. What does the user see, and what protects the origin when it comes back?
How do your nodes discover each other and communicate? What if I add a node?
You have heartbeats. So does the cluster detect a dead node?
You say you use weighted rendezvous hashing. Walk me through it. How does the weight enter, and what does the system do with it?
Walk me through a read. Which node serves it, and where does the hash come in?
You mention epochs. What is an epoch here, and does it give you a global version of the cache?
What if the invalidation message is lost or arrives late?
Can two of your nodes serve different values for the same key at the same time?
What happens if a node fails? What if the network partitions?
Your node protocol has a GET request. Can a peer poison your cache with it?
How accurate are your latency percentiles, and how do you compute them without slowing the request path?
How do you detect and handle hot keys?
How do you stop an unauthorised user reading or deleting cached data?
Your control endpoint changes cluster node state. Who can call it, and what stops a demo control from breaking production?
What happens if someone sends a malicious request: a huge body, a slow body, a crafted path?
How is tenant isolation enforced, and could one tenant ever see another's data?
How do you prevent resource exhaustion and protect the origin from overload?
Could a user make your gateway fetch an internal address (SSRF)?
What happens if an invalidation is lost or delayed? Can two nodes serve different values?
Is the system memory-safe, and how do you manage third-party risk?
How did you measure performance, and why should I trust the numbers?
Is your benchmark fair? Could you be fooling yourselves?
What would you improve first, and what are your real bottlenecks?
What is still unresolved? Give me the honest list.
Why not just use Redis or Memcached?
What is the actual intelligence in the system?
What is your strongest technical contribution?
Where are established products stronger than PhantomCache?
How would I reproduce one of your experiments?
What is the difference between your simulation and a real test?
You report that your adaptive controller failed. Why should I trust anything else?
What would you improve with more time?
What does "H1 NOT_SUPPORTED" actually say, and what does it not say?
A client sends DELETE and gets 204. Is that content guaranteed gone from every node?
Is this linearizable? What is your consistency model?
Can one tenant, or one cluster node, hurt another?
The sealed evaluation says H1 is NOT_SUPPORTED. What does that mean for your "intelligent" caching claim, and what happens to the product?
What would you do with more time?
What have you chosen not to claim, and what is untested?
Your repository is mostly uncommitted. Isn't that a process failure?
The README and an older handoff say the system passed a formal acceptance. Why do your records say otherwise?
